subject: Materials Science
title: UV Degradation of Polymers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: UV Degradation of Polymers.

hook.text: Leave a plastic chair in the sun for a year — it fades, cracks, and crumbles. UV light broke its chains.

buildup.text: UV photons have enough energy to break carbon-carbon bonds in polymer chains — a process called photodegradation.

discovery.text: Shorter chains mean lower molecular weight — the plastic becomes brittle, chalky, and loses strength.

twist.text: Carbon black absorbs UV before it reaches polymer bonds — that's why most outdoor plastics and tires are black.

climax.text: UV stabilizers like HALS (hindered amine light stabilizers) scavenge free radicals, extending outdoor life by decades.

punchline.text: Sunlight is a polymer's worst enemy — and a cheap additive is its best friend.

quiz.question: Why are most outdoor plastics and tires black?
options: Black color absorbs more heat, improving flexibility
Carbon black absorbs UV radiation, protecting the polymer chains
Black dyes are the cheapest available
